title: Microsoft Entra: Security Copilot agent for private application lifecycle management
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph incorrectly tells all customers outside Microsoft 365 E5 to purchase capacity, although Microsoft also documents included capacity for eligible E7 customers. The manual application-discovery recommendation also omits its Australia and Africa restriction. The roadmap facts match, and all four Learn links opened successfully.

claims.quote: Default Security Copilot Capacity is the automatically created inclusion capacity that appears in your tenant when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.

In Before rollout, change 'Microsoft 365 E5 default capacity' to 'Microsoft 365 E5 or E7 default inclusion capacity'.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The general Entra agent setup route is Microsoft Entra admin center > Agents > View details.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center ... Browse to Agents and select View details for the agent you want to configure.

claims.claim: Learn documents no API for turning on the Entra Security Copilot agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph API enable turn on Microsoft Entra Security Copilot agents configuration; Security Copilot agent Graph configuration enable. Read entra-agents and graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview; identity creation APIs do not document enabling these agents.

claims.claim: Security Copilot > Home menu > Owner settings > Security compute units is the capacity-control route.
claims.quote: go to the Home menu > Owner settings. ... Through the owner settings page: Under Security compute units or Number of overage units, select Change.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path as 'Home menu > Owner settings > Security compute units > Change'. In its note add: 'For overage, under Number of overage units select Change.' The current path stops on the correct page but before the action; both labels are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/manage-usage.

claims.claim: Learn documents no API operation for changing provisioned and overage Security Copilot SCU capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft.SecurityCopilot capacities REST API create update numberOfUnits overageUnits; Microsoft.SecurityCopilot/capacities; Security Copilot SCU capacity automation ARM REST update units API reference. Read manage-usage and SCU capacity; results name the resource but no setting operation.

claims.claim: Changing capacity in the Security Copilot portal requires Azure capacity Owner or Contributor and Security Copilot Owner.
claims.quote: Azure portal required role: Azure capacity owner or contributor. Security Copilot portal required role: Azure capacity owner or contributor who are also Security Copilot owners.

claims.claim: The SCU control manages general Security Copilot capacity consumed by agents, rather than setting capacity for this agent alone.
claims.quote: You consume SCUs ... Invoking Security Copilot through Microsoft-developed agents ... You can manage Security Copilot capacity by increasing or decreasing provisioned SCUs

claims.where: summary: its default and charges are not stated
claims.claim: Charges specific to this agent are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Application Lifecycle Management Agent SCU license; App Lifecycle Management Agent licensing permissions default. Read SCU capacity and manage-usage: no agent-specific per-run amount, but general SCU consumption and GA/public-preview charging are stated.
claims.fix: Replace 'its default and charges are not stated' with 'its default and per-run SCU consumption are not stated'. This preserves the narrow confirmed gap without suggesting that Security Copilot's general charging rules are unpublished.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, rescope applications
claims.claim: Microsoft advises rescoping discovery-created applications after validation, and the checklist extends that advice to agent-created applications.
claims.quote: new applications you create through application discovery inherit all assigned users and groups from Quick Access at creation. After you validate the new application, rescope the application's permissions

For agent-created applications, review whether their assignments match your intended access scope.' The second sentence is the wiki's advice, not an attribution to Microsoft's manual-discovery guidance.
